244	appointed over guarding the servants of Elokim.
245	But what the Radak says here at the beginning is that the acts of
246	God are carried out through intermediaries.
247	Meaning, behind this angel, since Yaakov
248	says, the Elokim,
249	the Elokim who sees me, the angel who redeems me. So
250	what does it mean that HaShem, so to speak, runs
251	creation through angels? And here we are
252	talking about a special domain of special angels
253	whose concern
254	is angels who guard the servants of HaShem.
255	In light of this we can understand
256	the nature of this angel being discussed here
257	in our Parashah, Mishpatim: "Behold, I send
258	an angel" — an emphasis that after you receive the Torah
259	you will continue to the Land of Israel and you will have
260	this accompaniment. But truthfully, it is not speaking
261	here of an angel who comes out of HaShem
262	being angry, as after the sin of the calf, when He says, I will not
263	be with you, I am sending a messenger, and then Moshe says to Him,
264	if Your presence does not go with us, do not take us up from here; we
265	want You to be with us too. Here it is still before
266	the calf, as I emphasized.
267	And there is an angel here, as there was with Avraham an angel,
268	and with Yitzchak an angel, and with Yaakov an angel, without any
269	sin.
270	Meaning, we have to make the distinction here
271	regarding this angel: the guardian angel is a
272	different angel; he does not come out of
273	a reaction to a situation of anger, God forbid, as it was after
274	the calf. This is what we need to understand now. Truthfully,
275	this angel is not actually mentioned for the first time
276	with regard to the people of Israel leaving Egypt here
277	in Parashat Mishpatim.
278	We probably did not notice it, but in fact it already appears
279	in Parashat Beshalach.
